title: Relative spectra preserve adequate moduli spaces
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ be an adequate moduli space [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space], and let $\mathcal B$ be a quasi-coherent commutative $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-algebra [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Use a common ambient universe $\mathcal U$ for schemes and the chart algebras: for every object $x$ of $\mathcal X$ over a $\mathcal U$-small scheme, the ring $\mathcal B(x)$ is $\mathcal U$-small (up to canonical size transport). Sites and compatible section families may live in a larger universe, as in [def-weil-size-convention]. The direct image $\phi_*\mathcal B$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-algebra. For a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal C$ on an algebraic stack or algebraic space $Z$, the relative spectrum $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Z\mathcal C$ means the functor of $\mathcal O_T$-algebra homomorphisms $u^*\mathcal C\to\mathcal O_T$ over objects $u:T\to Z$; on a scheme chart it is obtained by gluing affine spectra. These relative spectra are algebraic stacks, and the canonical map
$$\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{\mathcal X}\mathcal B\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_Y(\phi_*\mathcal B),$$
induced by evaluation $\phi^*\phi_*\mathcal B\to\mathcal B$, is an adequate moduli space. No finite-generation, flatness, or reducedness condition on $\mathcal B$ is required. Algebraic stacks and spaces use [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 5.2.11, printed p.28, and its use in Lemma 8.3.1, printed p.39. Read primary PDF online; local literature PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\phi_*\mathcal B$. The qcqs hypothesis in [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space] permits [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-algebra-direct-image]; its smooth-test formula, restricted to etale scheme tests of $Y$, identifies its quasi-coherent algebra with the direct image in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-relative-spec-construction] to obtain $q:V=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathcal X}\mathcal B\to\mathcal X$ affine and $p:Z=\operatorname{Spec}_Y\mathcal C\to Y$ an affine algebraic space. The evaluation $\phi^*\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$, followed on $V$ by the tautological evaluation to $\mathcal O_V$, gives $h:V\to Z$ over $Y$ by the defining functor of $Z$. Thus $p h=\phi q$, and $h$ is exactly the map in the statement.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 5.2.11, printed p.28; read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED. Expanded using the cited Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Choose an affine etale scheme cover $W_i\to Y$. Base change of the relative spectra in [lem-sfb-stack-relative-spec-construction] gives $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}_{\mathcal X_i}\mathcal B_i$ and $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}_{W_i}\mathcal C_i$, with $h_i:V_i\to Z_i$, where $\mathcal X_i=\mathcal X\times_YW_i$ and the subscript denotes tensor restriction. Such restrictions of quasi-coherent algebras are legitimate by [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction]. The etale-test formula of [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra] identifies $\mathcal C_i$ with $(\phi_i)_*\mathcal B_i$: on a scheme etale over $W_i$ the two values are sections over the same test stack. The composite test is etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. By [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality], $\phi_i$ is adequate. Write $R_i=\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal C_i)$. Then $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, and the structure-algebra and global-section identifications of [lem-sfb-stack-relative-spec-construction] give $R_i\simeq\Gamma(\mathcal X_i,\mathcal B_i)\simeq\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O_{V_i})$. The pullback of $h_i$ on global functions is this isomorphism: $c\in R_i$ is sent to its restriction to $\mathcal X_i$ followed by tautological evaluation on $V_i$.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 5.2.11, printed p.28; read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED. Expanded using the cited Stacks inputs.

proof.text: For the affine criterion we must check qcqs of $h_i$, rather than infer it from a desired moduli property. The morphism $\phi_i$ is qcqs by [def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space]. The morphisms $q_i:V_i\to\mathcal X_i$ and $W_i\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are affine (the first by [lem-sfb-stack-relative-spec-construction], the second because $W_i$ is an affine $k$-scheme). The affine and composition clauses of [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-composition-affine] make $V_i$ qcqs over $k$. Hence [lem-sfb-stack-affinization-qcqs] applies to $V_i$. The map $h_i$ of the preceding step, after the displayed identification $R_i\simeq\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal O)$, is its canonical affinization map: on every scheme object its algebra map is restriction of these global functions, as follows from the explicit evaluation description of $h_i$. The uniqueness clause of that node identifies these maps, so its qcqs conclusion proves $h_i$ qcqs.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 5.2.11, printed p.28; read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED. Expanded using the cited Stacks inputs.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal D\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal E$ be any surjection of quasi-coherent algebras on $V_i$ and let $t\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal E)$. Since $q_i$ is affine, [lem-sfb-stack-affine-algebra-direct-image] gives a surjection $(q_i)_*\mathcal D\twoheadrightarrow(q_i)_*\mathcal E$ of quasi-coherent algebras on $\mathcal X_i$ and natural ring identifications of its global sections with those on $V_i$. Apply the affine-target criterion of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] to the adequate $\phi_i:\mathcal X_i\to W_i$ and the section corresponding to $t$. It yields $N>0$ and a section of $(q_i)_*\mathcal D$ mapping to the $N$th power of that section. Transfer it back through the ring identifications to obtain $s\in\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal D)$ mapping to $t^N$. Those identifications preserve multiplication and powers, as the affine-direct-image node explicitly states. This argument quantifies over every algebra on $V_i$; none is assumed to be pulled back from $\mathcal X_i$.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Lemma 5.2.11, printed p.28; read online https://arxiv.org/pdf/1005.2398v3, local PDF WANTED. Expanded using the cited Stacks inputs.

proof.text: The affine-target criterion of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality], applied to $h_i:V_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, now uses exactly its qcqs property from step 3, the structural ring isomorphism from step 2 and the power lifts from step 4. It gives adequacy of every $h_i$. The family $Z_i=Z\times_YW_i\to Z$ is an etale cover by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Each $h_i$ is qcqs, so [lem-sfb-stack-etale-local-qcqs-homeomorphism] first gives qcqs of $h$. Etale locality of [lem-sfb-adequate-moduli-etale-locality] then gives adequacy of $h$. Quasi-coherence of $\mathcal C$ and algebraicity of both relative spectra were already proved in step 1. The construction and all cited inputs allowed arbitrary $\mathcal B$, so no finite-generation, flatness or reducedness hypothesis entered.

lean.statement:
theorem adequate_relative_spectrum {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (F : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))))
    (hF : IsAlgebraicModuliStack F) (Y : AlgebraicSpace (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    (φ : BasedFunctor F (discreteModuli Y.obj.obj))
    (hφ : IsAdequateModuliSpace F hF Y φ)
    (B : ModuliAlgebraSheaf F hF.1.1) (hB : IsQuasicoherentModuliAlgebra B)
    (hsmall : ∀ x : F.obj, Small.{u} (B.right.obj.obj (op x))) :
    ∃ (M : ModuliDirectImageAlgebraModel hF.1.1 Y φ B)
      (hV : IsAlgebraicModuliStack (moduliRelativeSpectrum B))
      (h : BasedFunctor (moduliRelativeSpectrum B)
        (discreteModuli (moduliImageRelativeSpectrum M).obj.left.obj.obj)),
      IsModuliRelativeSpecEvaluation φ B M h ∧
        IsAdequateModuliSpace (moduliRelativeSpectrum B) hV
          (moduliImageRelativeSpectrum M).obj.left h

statement_change.what: The recorded algebra-sheaf interface has coefficients in max (u+1) v w, whereas its algebraic stacks and spaces are tested only by Scheme.{u}. Quasi-coherence alone does not bound the cardinality of an algebra: over Spec k the polynomial algebra on a set larger than universe u is quasi-coherent, but its affine spectrum cannot be represented by a Scheme.{u}. Taking spectra therefore requires the ordinary common ambient-universe convention for schemes and chart algebras. The correction states exactly that size convention; it imposes no finiteness, flatness or reducedness. The already landed relative-Spec correspondence is added to name the target construction already present in the old statement.
